goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts the diff changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => { ... })` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })`. Since `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, any rejection from `await getCalendar(...)` (now async due to `await appStore[...]` dynamic import) or from `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`/`deleteMeeting(...)` will not be caught by the surrounding synchronous `try { ... } catch { ... }`, potentially leading to unhandled promise rejections and skipped cleanup. The same async-forEach pattern is also introduced elsewhere in the diff (e.g., wipemycalother and bookings router), reinforcing that this is a real behavioral issue introduced by the change.

adjudication.rationale: In CalendarManager.ts, getCalendar() is changed to async, but getCalendarCredentials still assigns `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` without awaiting, so the returned objects contain `calendar` as a Promise (verified by the diff). The in-file consumer `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `await item.calendar`, but this does change the shape/semantics of what getCalendarCredentials returns and could be surprising for other callers.
